newsitem.title: UK: UK NATURAL GAS MARKET BUSY, Q4 FALLS HARDEST.
newsitem.headline: UK NATURAL GAS MARKET BUSY, Q4 FALLS HARDEST.

text.p: The U.K. natural gas spot market was heavily traded on Wednesday, with all periods losing ground and the fourth quarter falling hardest.
After September slipped below the key nine pence a therm level on the IPE screen, October and November were both sold down on the spot market.
October traded at a low of 10.65 pence and November at 12.90 pence. The fourth quarter as a whole fell back to 13 pence.
"It was September falling below nine that gave us the bearish feeling," said one trader.
"September came right off and impacted on Q4. Q1 was also weaker but that has been trickling down for a while."
The first quarter traded slightly weaker at 16.85 pence.

The weakness was not confined to winter months, however, with summer gas marginally weaker at 10.70 pence. The market was active across the forward curve with trades seen as far ahead as the first quarter 1999.
